=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — buyer review

**Recommendation: do not accept the Seller’s package as drafted.** It would leave Wattlebridge paying the agreed AUD 24 million price while taking significant pre-Completion risks with limited recourse. The most important points are to secure Bluefen consent and a simultaneous Riverlark discharge, resolve the price treatment of debt and Completion bonuses, and prevent the general warranty limitations and disclosure provisions from neutralising protection for known risks.

This review is based on the Seller’s summary and Disclosure Letter, not the complete SPA or underlying due diligence documents. The actual wording and current evidence must be checked before positions are finalised.

## 1. Deal protection and Completion mechanics

### Bluefen — material customer consent

Bluefen reportedly generated approximately AUD 3.6 million of FY26 revenue, or 30% of revenue. No final consent or evidence that the conditions in clause 11.3 are satisfied is in the disclosed material.

**Push back:** Make Completion conditional on receiving Bluefen’s final written change-of-control consent **and satisfaction or express written waiver of all associated conditions**, on terms acceptable to the Buyer and without adverse variation to the contract. Require prompt evidence, active Seller cooperation and notice of any objection or proposed conditions. A written consent alone is insufficient if it remains conditional. Provide an appropriate long-stop date and termination right if the condition is not satisfied.

### Riverlark — debt and security

The approximately AUD 3.2 million facility remains outstanding, and a release after Completion is inconsistent with protecting the Buyer’s debt-free/cash-free bargain. Post-Completion, the Buyer could own a company still indebted and subject to security.

**Push back:** Require a current payout statement and binding discharge/release undertakings before Completion, with repayment and discharge occurring **simultaneously with Completion** through an agreed funds flow. Obtain releases of all relevant security and arrange necessary registrations. Ensure the debt is deducted from the amount otherwise payable to the Seller or paid on its behalf from the price, without double counting under the price adjustment. Do not rely on a later release.

### Completion bonuses — AUD 420,000 plus possible on-costs

The bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment and are omitted from the draft funds flow. Disclosure does not establish the payroll tax, superannuation or other on-cost treatment.

**Push back:** Establish who becomes liable, when each condition is satisfied, and the applicable on-costs. Require the Seller to fund the bonuses and attributable on-costs through the Completion funds flow, or provide a clear, equivalent price adjustment or reimbursement mechanism. Avoid double recovery. Check the treatment of employees who do not satisfy the conditions and any withholding obligations.

### Price mechanics and supplier renewals

The Seller asserts that the funds flow reflects the agreed mechanics, but the supplied materials do not establish how cash, debt, debt-like items and working capital are defined or adjusted. The three Sandbar renewals total AUD 330,000; their timing and whether they are avoidable, accrued or ordinary course are unresolved.

**Push back:** Reconcile the full funds flow and any completion accounts against the debt-free/cash-free agreement. Review DD-008 and DD-011 together, establish termination rights and accrual/payment dates, and allocate any pre-Completion or debt-like liability consistently with the agreed accounting definitions. Do not automatically deduct the full AUD 330,000 merely because it is disclosed; equally, do not accept the Seller’s ordinary-course characterisation without evidence.

## 2. Known risks requiring specific protection

### Ironquay IP

Transfer of the SOW3 project materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. An AUD 180,000 balance is recorded as open, but that is not conclusive proof of non-payment; there is no disclosed receipt or confirmatory assignment. The proposed indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment may not cover the consequences if Paperbark does not own or cannot use the relevant IP.

**Push back:** Before Completion, obtain independent evidence of cleared payment and an effective confirmatory assignment or other satisfactory chain-of-title evidence. Pending resolution, require a specific indemnity covering losses arising from the SOW3 payment and ownership or use of the relevant materials, including reasonable remediation, third-party claims and defence costs. It should not be confined to the invoice amount or subject to general warranty limits. Assess the commercial importance of the materials and whether a Completion condition is needed.

### Export/privacy incident

The facts establish that a link was sent to an unintended external address, not that an unauthorised person accessed the file or that a notifiable breach occurred. The scope, access and notification position remain under investigation; there is no established loss figure.

**Push back:** Require the Seller to preserve evidence, provide investigation updates and access to relevant records, and take appropriate containment steps. Obtain an agreed protocol for legal assessment, notification and remediation, including who controls communications and bears costs. Seek a specific indemnity for pre-Completion incident-related losses, investigation, legally required notification and remediation, with appropriate claim-control provisions and without general warranty limitations. Do not rely on a warranty alone where the matter is already disclosed.

### Tax and IP generally

Leaving tax and IP solely under the general regime could expose the Buyer to long-tail or high-impact liabilities after the 18-month period or above the proposed cap.

**Push back:** Seek a separate pre-Completion tax covenant/indemnity, appropriately covering liabilities attributable to pre-Completion periods, with a limitation period aligned to relevant assessment periods and agreed claim procedures. Seek substantive IP ownership, licence, infringement and chain-of-title warranties, with a longer survival period and a higher cap than ordinary business warranties. Preserve separate protection for Ironquay.

## 3. Warranty limitations, reliance and disclosure

### Caps, thresholds and survival

The Seller proposes a 20% general warranty cap (AUD 4.8 million), a claim threshold exceeding AUD 25,000, an excess-only AUD 250,000 basket, and 18 months’ survival. It also proposes applying limitations to every claim unless expressly excluded. Together, these terms significantly reduce recovery: qualifying claims are not recoverable until the basket is exceeded, and then only the excess is recoverable.

**Push back:** Negotiate a higher general cap, lower de minimis and basket, a **tipping basket** under which all qualifying losses are recoverable once the threshold is passed, and longer general warranty survival. The appropriate levels are commercial negotiation points. Ensure related losses can be aggregated so one underlying matter is not artificially fragmented.

Fundamental warranties—at least title, ownership and capacity—should not be subject to the general cap, thresholds or 18-month limit. Seek a cap up to the full purchase price and a materially longer period. Tax, specific indemnities and purchase-price/debt adjustments need their own expressly stated regimes. Preserve remedies for fraud and other non-excludable liability, and resist a blanket application of limitations to all claims.

### Exclusive remedy and non-reliance

Applying limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language to claims “of any nature” could undermine indemnities, price adjustments, Completion obligations and remedies for misrepresentation or deliberate misconduct.

**Push back:** Confine these provisions to a carefully defined scope. Expressly preserve claims under specific indemnities, debt and price-adjustment mechanics, Completion obligations, and appropriate equitable relief, as well as fraud and liability that cannot lawfully be excluded. Review the full interaction of clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 rather than relying on labels.

### General disclosure and Buyer knowledge

The Seller seeks to disclose the entire indexed data room, accounts, registers and public records, and to bar claims for matters known to the Buyer or advisers or merely discoverable. That could shift the burden of identifying and pricing undisclosed problems to the Buyer and render warranties ineffective.

**Push back:** Reject blanket data-room and public-record disclosure and the “discoverable” knowledge test. Permit disclosure only where a matter is **fairly disclosed**, with sufficient detail to identify its nature and scope and assess its implications against the relevant warranty. Limit any Buyer-knowledge qualification to actual knowledge of specifically identified individuals after reasonable enquiry; exclude imputed adviser knowledge and constructive knowledge. Neither disclosure nor knowledge should defeat the agreed specific indemnities or Completion protections unless expressly negotiated.

The Disclosure Letter’s reservations do not themselves resolve liability or establish that payments, consents or notifications are unnecessary. Conversely, disclosure of an issue is not proof that a breach or loss has occurred.

## 4. Title and remaining diligence

DD-012 identifies Harbourglass as the registered holder of 100% of issued shares, but does not independently verify the complete title position or establish freedom from encumbrances.

**Push back:** Verify the register, issued capital and corporate records; obtain searches and evidence concerning encumbrances and any options or other rights to shares. Require duly executed transfers, relevant corporate approvals, updated registers and release of any share security at Completion, supported by fundamental title warranties.

For **DD-007**, confirm and comply with the office lease notification obligation; the supplied material does not establish that landlord consent is required. For **Mossvale**, review the assignment restriction and transaction structure, but do not assume the share sale itself requires consent on the disclosed wording.

## Recommended priorities

1. **Make Bluefen consent and its conditions, and simultaneous Riverlark repayment and security release, Completion protections.**
2. **Reconcile the AUD 24 million debt-free/cash-free funds flow**, including the AUD 420,000 bonuses and on-costs, and investigate the Sandbar renewals.
3. **Resolve Ironquay title evidence and protect the Buyer against the export incident**, using tailored indemnities where the risks remain open.
4. **Separate fundamental, tax, IP and specific-indemnity protection from general warranty limits**; improve the general cap, basket and survival.
5. **Reject blanket disclosure, discoverability-based knowledge and all-claims remedy restrictions**, while preserving fraud and other applicable remedies.
6. **Verify share title and remaining contract obligations** against the underlying documents and complete SPA before signing.
